title: VPC deploy verifier: runtime sanity and burn-in simulator
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add an orchestration harness that runs after a VPC/private deployment to validate API readiness, perform model load concurrency checks, and execute a configurable burn-in simulation. This ticket builds a reusable runner that ties Terraform outputs -> probe inventory -> runtime verification -> results upload. Goals: (1) provide deterministic pass/fail signals for deploy gating, (2) exercise KV cache and model hot-start behavior across representative concurrency patterns, (3) surface regressions in runtime/kernel selection introduced by upgrades, and (4) document IaC hooks so upgrades can trigger the harness automatically.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New deploy verifier can be invoked from the deployment pipeline and returns a machine-readable status (PASS/FAIL) and a short failure reason.
2) The runner executes: basic API handshake, model load (cold), sustained token generation at 1/5/10 concurrent clients for 5 minutes each, and a final smoke prompt set that validates structured output.
3) Results are uploaded to S3 + a per-deploy dashboard link is emitted to the deploy summary.
4) Terraform module outputs include a boolean flag to opt-in to run the harness after upgrades.
5) Observability traces and token-level latency percentiles are captured and stored for regression comparisons.
steps: Design harness interface and schema for results (JSON with metrics + verdict)
Implement probe runners: api-handshake, model-load, concurrency-generator, structured-smoke
Add Terraform module output: harness_endpoint, harness_token, run_on_upgrade_flag
Integrate with existing post-deploy orchestration (orchestration-probe-runner) via invocation from the pipeline
Wire results upload to S3 and emit dashboard link to deploy summary in the CI job
Add baseline regression job to compare current run with last successful run and flag large regressions
Create runbook for on-call to triage harness failures and common remediation steps
notes: Prototype focuses on Llama2-13B and Mistral-7B-lite model shapes used by internal staging clusters.
Decision: use existing 'probe-chain' library for request sequencing to avoid rewriting retry and backoff logic.
Trade-off: longer burn-in durations (10m) increase deployment latency; default to 5m with override for release trains.
Security: harness credentials scoped to a single deploy bucket and limited API token lifetime (15m).
If the harness fails due to transient infra flakiness, pipeline should allow a single automatic re-run before marking upgrade as failed.
